newsitem.title: USA: IBM unveils set-top box design kit.
newsitem.headline: IBM unveils set-top box design kit.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp said it unveiled a board with chips and software for a new set top box design, to help television set-top box developers get their products to market more quickly.

The board design, which IBM said is called a reference design kit, is the first step in IBM's plan to develop a custom chip that blends set-top box functions into one single chip. Currently, the board contains three different chips.
The kit contains some IBM parts and some industry standard components for set-top box makers. The kit will be available in June at a price of $7,500.
IBM said its set-top box design kit also includes software components that lets equipment manufacturers focus on developing their own customized functions.

IBM said that major set-top box makers like Thomson Consumer Electronics, a unit of Thomson SA and Tatung Co Ltd have already selected IBM designs, based on IBM's PowerPC chip, to power their upcoming boxes.

Currently, the board includes a PowerPC RISC processor, an IBM audio/video decoder chip to display video, play audio, and control on-screen display. It also has a set-top box peripheral chip to integrate devices such as a modem or a PC.
